newsitem.title: USA: Stocks set sixth straight record, bond rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Stocks set sixth straight record, bond rates fall.

text.p: Stocks capped a record-breaking week with a broad-based rally Friday, and bonds and the dollar rose after a new report showed inflation well under control.

The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 70.57 points, or 0.9 percent, to 7,782.04, its sixth consecutive record. With Friday's advance, the Dow has risen 477 points, or 6.5 percent, in the past six sessions.
For the week, the Dow rose a record 346.26 points, topping the rise of 332 points set the week ended May 2.
"It's just sort of a classic buying panic," said John Church, chief investment officer at Glenmede Trust Co.
Reflecting the breadth of the rally, rising issues beat losers by 1,724 to 814 on heavy volume of 566.9 million on the New York Stock Exchange.
After lagging for most of the week, the Nasdaq composite index joined in and rose 11.71 points to 1,423.03, a record. The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 9.79 points to a record 893.27.

The latest catalyst for stocks was a report of an unexpected drop in wholesale prices for May, the fifth consecutive monthly decline. The Labour Department said the Producer Price Index fell 0.3 percent in May after a 0.6 percent fall in April. Economists had forecast that the index edged higher in May.

The data, coupled with other recent statistics including Thursday's report on soft May retail sales, indicate little sign of inflation that could spur the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates, analysts said.
The data "is going to make it very difficult for the Fed to raise rates," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford.
The dollar rose broadly Friday as investors shunned the German mark and bought dollars amid concern that the planned single European currency might end up being weaker than expected.

Comments from officials attending a Franco-German summit Friday suggested an agreement was imminent on a European Union stability pact that would outline budgetary requirements for members of Europe's proposed single currency, the euro.

"The dollar gained from continued expectations in the market that there is going to be some kind of an agreement within the EU nations this weekend that will probably lead to a slightly weaker euro," said Stephen Jury, chief dealer at Union Bank of Switzerland.
The dollar rose to 1.7353 marks from 1.7290 at Thursday's close and to 114.80 Japanese yen from 114.20.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury rose 20/32, or $6.25 on a $1,000 bond, sending its yield down to 6.73 percent from 6.78 percent on Thursday. The price and the yield move in opposite directions.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, July crude oil rose 14 cents to $18.83 a barrel. On New York's Commodity Exchange, August gold fell 50 cents to $343.10 an ounce.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index rose to its third record this week, ending at 4,783.1, up 25.7 points. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,528.35, down 36.11 points.
